## Purpose
Implements `POST /api/runs/{id}/files` (UPLD-01), the endpoint a run's owner uses to attach documents to an in-flight or reopened run. Accepted files are written under the run's on-disk `RunSandbox` at a reserved `.uploads/` prefix, with extractable types (pdf/docx/pptx) getting a `.txt` sidecar and a `manifest.json` entry so the uploaded text stays available to the agent on every subsequent turn.

## Shape
- `upload_files` — the single route handler; does the two-layer owner check (ORM filter on `WorkflowRun.user_id` → 404, then a default-deny `ScopedStore.get_run` re-check → 404), validates every file up front (ext allow-list, per-file/aggregate byte caps, document count cap), then persists.
- `_read_capped` — streams each multipart part in bounded chunks, aborting once it crosses the per-file cap, so an over-cap upload is never fully buffered before rejection.
- `_dedupe_segment` — appends a `-N` suffix when two distinct filenames sanitize to the same on-disk name, so a later upload never silently clobbers an earlier one.
- `_manifest_lock` — a POSIX advisory file lock (no-op on Windows) that serializes the manifest read-merge-write across concurrent requests/processes, preventing a last-write-wins loss of manifest entries.
- `_write_bytes` / `_read_manifest` — small helpers for writing raw bytes through `RunSandbox.path_for` and loading the existing manifest as a name-keyed map.
- After caps pass and files are written, the handler also best-effort mirrors each extracted-text sidecar plus the manifest snapshot as `artifact_refs` rows (via `ScopedStore.write_ref`), so a resumed run whose sandbox was wiped still has its uploaded-document context; a `SQLAlchemyError` here is logged and swallowed, anything else re-raised.

## Why this shape
The module's own docstring and inline comments name the constraints driving this structure directly: caps must be enforced before any sandbox write (so a single rejected file never leaves partial state on disk), all sandbox writes must resolve through `RunSandbox.path_for` to stay traversal-proof, and the owner check must mirror `run_commands.post_message` exactly so the two ingress paths can't diverge on ownership semantics.
